item.title: Broadband soliton microcombs in the biological window enabled by a resonant coupler
item.description: arXiv:2610.12603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband soliton microcombs near 1 $\mu$m offer coherent, evenly spaced optical lines for measurements in the biological window. However, combining broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines increases the pump-power requirement and makes thermally stable soliton access more difficult. Here, we demonstrate broadband silicon nitride (Si3N4) soliton microcombs enabled by a resonant coupler that enhances pump delivery to the nonlinear resonator. The device generates a spectrum spanning 930-1380 nm with an approximately 98-GHz comb-line spacing at on-chip pump powers of tens of milliwatts, while providing reliable thermally stable access to the single-soliton state. These results provide a route to compact, power-efficient microcomb sources that combine broad spectral coverage with closely spaced comb lines for spectroscopy and imaging in the biological window.
item.dc:creator: Xinrui Luo, Du Qian, Yuanlei Wang, Yiwen Yang, Kaixuan Zhu, Yinke Cheng, Haoyang Luo, Junqi Wang, Bei-Bei Li, Qihuang Gong, Qi-Fan Yang

item.title: Coherent ultraviolet frequency combs generated by resonant dispersive waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.12620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant dispersive wave (RDW) emission in gas-filled anti-resonant hollow-core fibers (AR-HCF) offers a wavelength-tunable route to ultraviolet (UV) and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) frequency comb generation. RDW emission is expected to be coherent fundamentally, but various noise sources are expected to limit the coherence, including amplitude-to-phase fluctuations due to input pulse intensity noise and plasma formation. It is critical, therefore, to establish the limits of the coherence of UV RDW pulses to determine their applicability for precision spectroscopy. Here, we demonstrate the coherence of RDW emission at 260~nm generated with an amplified Yb-doped fiber system at a 2-MHz repetition rate with a self-heterodyne beat measurement between the RDW and the fourth harmonic of the source. We isolate the RDW contribution to the frequency noise by coherently subtracting the carrier-envelope offset noise contribution measured simultaneously with an f-2f interferometer. We observe a beatnote linewidth below 10~kHz over timescales longer than 100~ms, and we find a conservative upper bound of 1~rad on the integrated RMS phase deviations over a frequency range spanning 1 to 30~kHz. The dominant frequency noise contributions are consistent with environmental noise of the interferometers and AR-HCF coupling fluctuations. These results provide strong evidence that RDW emission is coherent under well-controlled experimental conditions, confirming its potential for UV and VUV frequency comb generation.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hemsworth, Arthur K. Mills, Christina Hofer, TJ Hammond, David J. Jones

item.title: Theory of Disorder-Induced Multimode Coupling in a Fabry-P\'erot Cavity
item.description: arXiv:2610.12687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong light--matter interactions have attracted significant interest in physical chemistry due to the potential for modifying molecular processes by hybridizing with cavity photons and forming polaritonic states. However, for a disordered molecular ensemble within an optical cavity capable of supporting multiple photon modes, theoretical understanding of multimode polaritons remains incomplete, particularly regarding whether and how distinct photon modes are mutually coupled through molecules. In this work, we generalize the collective mode expansion formalism to incorporate multiple photonic modes and show that spatial and orientational disorder in the light--matter coupling strength (originating from dipole orientation fluctuations and photonic field inhomogeneity) can mediate cross-mode coupling. This disorder-induced coupling allows for energy transfer to otherwise unexcited photon modes through a mechanism termed disorder-induced multimode activation (DIMA). Using an effective one-dimensional Fabry--P\'erot cavity as a test system, we demonstrate that the cross-mode energy transfer through DIMA can be controlled by changing the molecular layer thickness and the optical properties of the mirrors. Furthermore, we show that DIMA is robust against weak energetic disorder. This mechanistic understanding lays the foundation for a systematic control of multimode photon coupling using disorder-induced effects.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Kuo Li, Hsing-Ta Chen

item.title: Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor: Phase Contrast with Engineered Focal Plane Reference Speckles
item.description: arXiv:2610.12807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor (phantom ZWFS), an engineered reference extension of phase-contrast wavefront sensing in which controlled pupil plane modulation generates off-axis coherent speckle structures that undergo localized focal plane phase shifts. These references may replace the central ZWFS reference when the on-axis PSF core is required for another optical function, such as photonic science coupling, or may augment a conventional central ZWFS response to provide additional wavefront information. Using a monochromatic scalar model, we derive the resulting carrier structure and show how the engineered references can be recovered through spatial demodulation and incorporated into calibrated reconstruction. A simple four-reference realization demonstrates that the reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, producing mode dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than a uniform improvement over a classical ZWFS. We then consider differential piston on a seven segment aperture as an application specific example. A hybrid sensor retaining the central ZWFS phase region and adding six engineered references that match the segment geometry gives similar precision near the phased state but substantially improved performance at larger piston excursions. Under the adopted photon-noise-limited benchmark, the hybrid reduces the nonlinear reconstruction error and provides better conditioned optical encoding of the piston state than an idealized vector ZWFS, allowing more precise piston estimation from the same detected photon flux at larger piston excursions.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Courtney-Barrer

item.title: Topologically steerable ultra-flat electro-optic combs via non-Hermitian frequency lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.12867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electro-optic (EO) frequency combs convert microwave signals to the optical domain with deterministic repetition rates, enabling applications in optical telecommunications, microwave photonics, and LiDAR. However, generating flat EO combs has remained a long-standing challenge due to exponential decay of the spectral envelope inherent to bidirectional frequency coupling within conventional schemes. Here we reveal the inherent correspondence between flat-comb generation and the topological energy bands of non-Hermitian nonreciprocal frequency lattices, and experimentally realize ultra-flat combs with topologically controlled spectral flow. We derive the exact analytical condition for flat-comb generation, and find that it maps precisely onto the complex energy band, thereby establishing a direct connection between comb-envelope engineering and non-Hermitian topology. Experimentally, we observe an ultra-flat comb whose frequency evolution direction is governed by the topological winding and remains robust against detuning and phase fluctuations. This scheme can be further extended to long-range coupling and multi-lattice architectures, underscoring its versatility for flat dual- and multi-comb generation. Our work establishes a topologically steerable approach for achieving ultra-flat EO combs, paving the way for chip-scale spectral engineering via non-Hermitian topology.
item.dc:creator: Weiwei Liu, Xiaolong Su, Bing Wang, Yongjie Wang, Pang Fu, Wenxian Zhang, Ruiqian Cheng, Songpan Hong, Qingbin Zhang, Peixiang Lu

item.title: Silent breakdown of the perturbative polarization expansion in the terahertz regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.12982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear optics expands the polarization in powers of the drive and retains only the lowest-order terms. This truncation is safe at optical frequencies, where the convergence field lies far above the damage threshold. In the terahertz regime, phonon polaritons enhance the nonlinear susceptibilities by orders of magnitude, lowering the convergence field into the sub-damage range and opening a window in which the expansion fails while the crystal remains recoverable. We term this window silent breakdown. At resonance, the nearest singularities of the driven lattice mode are a complex-conjugate pair of branch points below the multistability threshold, so the response remains smooth and single-valued even though the $\chi^{\left( n \right)}$ description fails. The convergence field scales as $Q^{-3/2}$, so sharpening a resonance enhances the nonlinearity but narrows the range over which the expansion applies. It follows from the mode shift $S$ alone, $E_{\mathrm{conv}}=E_{\mathrm{ref}}(3\sqrt{3}QS)^{-1/2}$, giving 2$\sim$9 MV/cm for $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{3}$. Since resonant enhancement is central to terahertz nonlinear optics, this boundary defines the field range over which susceptibility-based descriptions are quantitatively reliable.
item.dc:creator: Yao Lu, Jiawei Zhang, Qiang Wu, Jingjun Xu

item.title: Matrix-free numerical continuation of the Ikeda map in passive Kerr resonators
item.description: arXiv:2610.12994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a matrix-free numerical continuation framework for the Ikeda map of coherently driven passive Kerr resonators. The framework traces solution branches and evaluates their linear stability without explicitly assembling the full Jacobian matrices, using a unified formulation for states that recur after one or multiple round trips. We resolve stable and unstable branches of modulation-instability patterns and temporal cavity solitons, and uncover period-doubled homogeneous states and associated multi-round-trip dynamics that are absent from the standard Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE). For period-1 states, the Ikeda map and the LLE show close agreement in the high-finesse regime, while their branch-existence intervals increasingly deviate as the finesse decreases. These results demonstrate that direct continuation of the unaveraged round-trip map can capture nonlinear states and multi-round-trip dynamics beyond the mean-field description, providing a systematic framework for bifurcation and stability analysis of Kerr resonators without relying on the averaged LLE.
item.dc:creator: Yuandi Xu, Pengxiang Wang, Jianxing Pan, Haisu Zhang, Gang Xu

item.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
item.description: arXiv:2610.13381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. Based on these findings, we propose a SERS-active system that provides strong signal enhancement (up to four orders of magnitude for a single globular object) while maintaining spectral fidelity, where PMSs act both as model analytes and as integral components of a metal-dielectric resonator.
item.dc:creator: Andrey K. Sarychev, Milena S. Shestopalova, Denis S. Korzhov, Andrey V. Ivanov, Igor V. Bykov, Konstantin N. Afanasev, Nikita N. Osipov, Dmitry V. Basmanov, Vladimir A. Oleinikov, Konstantin E. Mochalov

item.title: Localization Landscapes based on the Green's Matrix of Non-Hermitian Optical Scattering Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Filoche--Mayboroda (FM) localization landscape predicts where the spatially localized modes of a self-adjoint elliptic operator reside without diagonalizing it, but the construction fails for the complex, non-normal Green's matrix G of an open scattering array of electric dipoles. We propose three real-valued, positive landscapes built from the Feinberg--Zee hermitization of G: a regularised Gramian inverse (Gram), the diagonal Schur block that carries the Metz--Neri--Rogers spectral density (SY), and the full hermitized inverse contracted against a polarization-isotropic source pair (Herm). The three form a progression from spectrum-blind to fully hermitisation-faithful, agree in the limit $z\to 0$, and diverge where it matters: at nonzero spectral shift SY resolves modes that Gram collapses, and Herm resolves modes that SY collapses. We demonstrate the progression on random and deterministic aperiodic scattering arrays with a wide range of structural correlations, extend to the vectorial case of transverse electric polarization (TE), and provide rigorous justifications along with mathematical proofs and a complete numerical recipe in the appendices and in the supplementary material.
item.dc:creator: Luca Dal Negro, Hari Sundar

item.title: Spectral-control-assisted Kerr-lens mode-locking in a Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser
item.description: arXiv:2610.13427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser stabilized by suppressing wavelength competition under high population-inversion conditions. The laser delivers an average output power of 0.5 W with a pulse duration of 112 fs at a repetition rate of 90 MHz and a central wavelength of 2.08 um. Further optimization for shorter pulses yields a pulse duration of 107 fs, through with a reduced output power of 0.22 W. These results demonstrate that spectral-control is an effective approach for achieving stable mode-locking in such laser with strong spectral competition.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Gong, Jing Wang, Panqiang Kang, Weichao Yao, Yujie Peng, Jun Wang, Dingyuan Tang, Yuxin Leng

item.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
item.description: arXiv:2610.13525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. The chip is opto-electronic and features co-packaged electronics using tiny electronic chiplets that are bonded to the sapphire. These consist of an LD driver and transimpedance amplifier for the UV photonics, together with ASICs, ADC, microcontroller, micro-battery and RF-wireless or Ethernet chiplets. The mission of this self-contained cost-effective chip is sensing targeted medical-chemical-biological (MCB) agents in a local or network setting. Eight significant MCB applications are detailed here.
item.dc:creator: Richard Soref

item.title: Aubry-Andr\'e transition in photonic time quasicrystals
item.description: arXiv:2610.13538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-Andr\'e model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-Andr\'e transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-Andr\'e transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.
item.dc:creator: Shuhang Chen, Qi Zhu

item.title: Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials. These findings open a new avenue for designing nonlinear chiroptical crystals which harness the duality of polarity and chirality and chemical versatility of COFs.
item.dc:creator: Yile Zhang, Lei Wei, Sixue Tang, Yuhang Li, Yanhang Ma, Yue-Biao Zhang, Xiaoqin Shen

item.title: PhySeqNet: physics-informed fluorescent foci detection for BARseq spatial transcriptomics
item.description: arXiv:2610.13779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: BARseq enables spatially resolved gene-expression profiling across intact tissue, but its sensitivity depends on accurate detection and decoding of dense fluorescent rolonies. Existing spot-calling approaches can be conservative where signals overlap, while supervised deep learning is limited by the lack of reliable manual ground truth in real tissue images. Here we present PhySeqNet, a physics-informed deep learning framework for annotation-free fluorescent foci detection in BARseq. PhySeqNet trains U-Net detectors entirely on semi-synthetic images generated from an instrument-matched optical model combined with real sample-free experimental noise, and is integrated into pyBARseq, a modular Python pipeline for BARseq analysis. PhySeqNet achieved high detection performance on held-out simulated data across wavelength bands. On real tissue images, where ground truth is unavailable, we evaluated detections by forward-model reconstruction: PhySeqNet with conservative barcode-aware non-maxima suppression (NMSB) achieved higher reconstruction fidelity (NCC and MS-SSIM) than the BarDensr single-shot estimator, tuned classical spot detectors, and a pretrained deep-learning detector. In the analyzed brain section, PhySeqNet with NMSB yielded a median of 51 counts per cell versus 47 for BarDensr, with a similar number of genes detected per cell. The recovered transcripts produced spatial expression patterns qualitatively consistent with Allen MERFISH reference data and preserved cell-type composition after scANVI label transfer. These results show that physics-informed simulation can train practical, annotation-free detectors that improve BARseq sensitivity without disrupting downstream biological interpretation.
item.dc:creator: Neha Goswami (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, Cold Spring Harbor, NY, USA), John Hover (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, Cold Spring Harbor, NY, USA), Renae Galluccio (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, Cold Spring Harbor, NY, USA), Yichen Wu (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, Cold Spring Harbor, NY, USA), Huiqing Zhan (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, Cold Spring Harbor, NY, USA), Xiaoyin Chen (Allen Institute for Brain Science, Seattle, WA, USA), Anthony M. item.title: Statistical Optical Replication and Mixing of Spatial Information across Wavelengths
item.description: arXiv:2610.13861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accessing and combining the spatial information carried by light at different wavelengths is important for linking structured-light encoding with spectrally distinct detection channels. Here, we introduce a correlation-enabled linear-optical framework for cross-wavelength imaging, bidirectional replication, and spatial information mixing. Shared random holographic modulation establishes correlations between nondegenerate optical fields, allowing spatial information to be retrieved from joint intensity fluctuations. In the demonstrated replicator, a spatial pattern encoded at one wavelength is read out in the detection coordinates of another through intensity correlations. Selecting diffraction-order pairs produces correlation kernels containing either the product or the conjugate product of two input field envelopes. These operations reproduce the spatial algebra underlying sum- and difference-frequency generation, while the optical fields retain their original carrier frequencies. The theory accounts for wavelength-dependent propagation and coordinate scaling, linking the input structures to observable correlation patterns. Together, these results establish a common framework for cross-wavelength spatial information processing through engineered optical correlations and joint detection.
item.dc:creator: Wanting Hou, Wei Liu, Hong-Chao Liu, Zhiyuan Ye, Jun Xiong

item.title: Optimal linear-optical interferometers for unitary t-designs in a multi-photon Fock space
item.description: arXiv:2610.12646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the construction of unitary $t$-designs in a multi-photon Fock space on programmable linear-optical interferometers. Using the frame potential as the optimization objective, we identify architectures that realize approximate unitary 1- and 2-designs with considerably fewer controllable parameters than required for universal linear optics. For example, we find numerical evidence suggesting that for unitary 1-designs, the required number of programmable parameters scales empirically as $2d$ with the number of modes $d$, instead of $O(d^2)$. We benchmark the resulting ensembles using single-photon transition probabilities and average channel fidelities. Furthermore, as a practical result, we develop a photon-number estimation protocol for multi-photon Fock states that leverages these optimized 1- and 2-designs. Our findings demonstrate that shallow interferometers can accurately reproduce Haar-averaged first moments, while second-moment-sensitive observables provide a considerably stricter test for approximate unitary 2-designs.
item.dc:creator: Robert A. Grinshtein, Ivan V. Dyakonov, Stanislav S. Straupe

item.title: Quantum Information-Theoretic Analysis of Optical Fiber Sensing via Stimulated Brillouin Scattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.12980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. Assuming the input probe is a quantum state, we develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for SBS-based fiber sensing and intrusion detection. Starting from a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian, we derive an effective input-output relation for a short fiber segment. We then model each fiber segment as a single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel and the entire fiber as a cascade of quantum channels. We then compute the quantum Fisher information for general SBS-dependent parameters and identify optimal measurement settings to achieve the quantum limit, comparing them with receiver-constrained strategies such as heterodyne detection and photon counting. In addition, we propose an adaptive approach that achieves first-order asymptotic optimality and provides a novel second-order correction to address preliminary miscalibration. As an application, we apply the framework to the fiber-tapping detection problem.
item.dc:creator: Kiran Adhikari, Janis N\"otzel

item.title: All-optical deconvolution via quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy with bright twin beams
item.description: arXiv:2610.13074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. Employing the signal beam as a broadband probe, QCCS achieves all-optical deconvolution through a correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation channel between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams. By subtracting the uncorrelated background using a 500-femtosecond temporal window, we successfully retrieve narrow Raman bands (8 cm^{-1} and 15 cm^{-1}) completely obscured by a 75 cm^{-1} probe bandwidth without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge. Our results establish macroscopic quantum correlations as a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, paving the way for ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural, incoherent excitation conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yujiro Eto

item.title: Solitons in the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with the pseudo-Raman term, anti-diffusion gain and nonlinear loss
item.description: arXiv:2610.13255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a nonconservative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLSE) which includes additional nonlinear terms accounting for the pseudo-stimulated-Raman-scattering (pseudo-SRS) effect and cubic loss. An essentially novel feature of the model is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which leads to the obvious blow-up in the infinite or spatially periodic system. We consider the absorptive boundary conditions, which suppress the blow-up driven by effective convective instability in the setup. The NSLE model is derived, in the extended adiabatic approximation, from the underlying Zakharov system, which includes the viscosity term acting on its low-frequency component and the anti-diffusion gain in the high-frequency (HF) one. The latter term appears if the expansion, with respect to the deviation of the wavenumber, is performed not around the minimum-loss point (as in the usual situation), but around a maximum-loss point. Dynamics of moving solitons in the model is addressed by means of analytical and numerical methods. The sech approximation for the soliton predicts it as a stable fixed point (FP) of the system of balance equations for the HF norm and wave momentum, derived in the moving reference frame. The FP attraction basin is identified too. The predictions are corroborated by direct simulations of the full NSLE with the absorptive boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny M. Gromov, Boris A. Malomed

item.title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.13664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu$^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition at $\sim$580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C$_1$, C$_2$) yields higher branching ratios of the $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition, exceeding 1\% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of $T_{\text{2}}^{\text{opt}} = 2.3~\mu\mathrm{s}$ at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Lester Jobbitt, Sascha Weis, Timo Schweizer, Vishnu Unni Chorakkunnath, Evgenij Vasilenko, Tobias Haas, Barbora Brachnakova, Senthil Kumar Kuppusamy, Hartmut Schubert, Mario Ruben, Michael Seitz, David Hunger

item.title: Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
item.description: arXiv:2511.02440v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ultrafast all-optical magnetization switching (AOS) holds great promise for nextgeneration spintronic memory and hybrid spintronic-photonic systems. However, most implementations to date rely on bulky free-space optical setups, limiting scalability and practical integration. As a critical step toward integrated applications, we demonstrate single-pulse AOS within a silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuit. Using trains of femtosecond laser pulses guided through on-chip waveguides, we achieve deterministic toggle switching in a sub-micron out-of-plane Co/Gd Hall cross patterned directly atop the photonic waveguide. Electrical readout via the anomalous Hall effect reveals a switching contrast of up to 90% for 500 nm-wide devices. In larger Hall crosses, the contrast decreases and switching becomes stochastic, consistent with spatially non-uniform optical absorption as confirmed by finite-element simulations. This behavior is hypothetically attributed to domain wall relaxation and thermally assisted (de)pinning processes within partially switched regions. Our results highlight the critical role of device scaling in achieving robust on-chip AOS and establish a foundation for ultrafast, energy-efficient, and fully integrated spintronic-photonic platforms.
item.dc:creator: Pingzhi Li, Gijs W. A. Simons, Tianyu Zhang, Philip P. J. Schrinner, Sohrab Kamyar, Ronald Dekker, Diana C. Leitao, Reinoud Lavrijsen, Yuqing Jiao, Bert Koopmans

item.title: Bounds on Propagation Constants in Dielectric Gratings
item.description: arXiv:2609.05052v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish analytical bounds on the normalized longitudinal propagation constants $\beta=k_z/k_0$ of modes in lossless dielectric diffraction gratings. If $\epsilon_{\max}$ denotes the maximum relative permittivity, we show that regular modes ($\beta^2\in\mathbb{R}$) satisfy $\beta^2\le\epsilon_{\max}$ despite the lack of a scalar dispersion relation. We further show that the so-called ghost modes ($\beta^2\notin\mathbb{R}$), admitted by the non-Hermitian nature of the associated eigenproblem, satisfy $|\mathrm{Re}(\beta)|\le\sqrt{\epsilon_{\max}}/2$. Both bounds are obtained directly from the Fourier-series formulation of the fully coupled vectorial eigenproblem.
item.dc:creator: Ehsan Faghihifar

item.title: Field Angular Momentum Transformation as a Resolution Criterion for Microsphere-assisted microscopy
item.description: arXiv:2609.17214v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a sequential analysis of the resolving power of a microparticle as a function of its refractive index and size parameter. We demonstrate that the resolution of a microparticle for incoherent point sources is fundamentally determined by the number of excited Mie modes. Based on this mechanism, we propose a novel quantitative assessment framework that defines the spatial resolution limit via the ratio of the squared field angular momentum of the source to that of the total particle field (comprising the superposition of the source and scattered fields). The analytical results demonstrate good agreement with both numerical modeling and classical limits.
item.dc:creator: Bekirov Arlen

item.title: Bogoliubov-de Gennes spectrum, Cherenkov radiation and recoil of solitons with third-order dispersion underlying optical analogue horizons
item.description: arXiv:2610.09814v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Third-order dispersion turns the soliton of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, which underlies optical analogues of event horizons in fibers, into a weakly radiating solitary wave. We compute three of its properties without assuming a thermal emission law. First, the linearized (Bogoliubov-de Gennes) problem must be posed about the stationary state of the dispersive equation: linearizing about the integrable profile produces a complex quartet that is converged in grid and box, grows as the square root of the dispersion strength and is spurious. About the stationary state, on a periodic grid, the zero-mode sector consists of two Jordan blocks of size two and the spectrum is real at the operating point, including negative-energy box modes of the resonant branch. Second, we measure the steady Cherenkov emission of adiabatically prepared solitons from the flux of the radiation behind them, over eight decades. The radiation is phase-matched in the frame of the drifting soliton, and the first-order rate falls short of the measured one by factors of 29 to 45. Expressed through a scaled dispersion coefficient of the local soliton, the measured rate describes launched solitons of three amplitudes; with norm and momentum balance, and no further fitted parameter, it reproduces their recoil and the slow decay of their loss rate; at weak dispersion the loss of a launched soliton is the shedding of its launch mismatch. Third, a census of the asymptotic channels shows that long-wavelength upstream emission requires the chemical potential of the soliton, lowered by the comoving-frame Doppler shift of a drifting soliton, to lie inside the analysis band, which bounds the soliton amplitude. In a kinematic model of the flow the surface gravity has a closed form; the thermal relation and the entanglement built on it are imposed inputs of that model. The construction applies to Raman-free Kerr media.
item.dc:creator: Hasan Oguz
